report.summary: The app already behaves as NTF-1 and NTF-2 require, so I changed no code. The server returns notifications for the signed-in account only: `server.mjs:61` looks up `notifications[account.user]`. The signed-in account is `dana`, and `data/notifications.json` has `"dana": []`, so she has no notifications. Under NTF-2, an account with none should see "You're all caught up", and that is what she sees. Only `lee` has notifications (n-201 and n-202). The client in `public/src/notifications.js` lists whatever the API returns, newest first. It shows the error message and Retry button only when the read fails, and never shows the empty message in that case. I found no bug in the account lookup, the API, the client or the sorting. If Dana really should have notifications, they are missing from the data, which is a data or upstream question and not a code defect. I changed nothing because I can't tell what she should be seeing.
report.verification: I read `server.mjs`, `public/src/notifications.js`, `api.js`, `format.js`, `main.js` and the data files. `npm test` passes all 4 tests, including the one for newest-first ordering. I did not drive the page in a browser.
